title: Negative-question order with plural owners
focus: Build plural-owner negative questions: eikö + owner + ole + partitive thing.
prerequisiteSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions

exercises.prompt: Build “Don’t we have a book?” Put the owner immediately after the question word. Use meillä (“we as the owner”) and kirjaa (“a book”).
exercises.explanation: Follow the pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun.
requiredSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
Negative possession question word order
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Negative possession question word order: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun

parts.formation: Ei + the question ending -kö = eikö. The front-vowel ending follows ei, independently of the noun.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: me has the learned possession form meillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Negative possession keeps ole after eikö, with every owner.
kirja + -a = kirjaa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

optionFeedback.Eikö meillä ole koiraa?: Use eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun.
